endorsements.quote: This argues for controlled testing environments, including shadow-mode evaluation, error injection, and clearly documented conceptual boundaries between method development, internal decision support, and regulated clinical decision tools.
Evaluation criteria, minimum sample size where possible, duration, and the threshold for progression to production should be specified at the outset.

Organizations should therefore invest deliberately in upskilling drug safety professionals to interpret model outputs, understand the assumptions on which those outputs rest, and recognize the conditions under which they should not be relied upon.
Formal data pipelines and change control are also essential so that model updates, feature changes, retraining, and threshold modifications remain reviewable, traceable, and auditable.
Equally important is inspection-ready documentation of data origin, assumptions, uncertainty, and decision implications to preserve transparency and scientific defensibility.
Predictive safety should therefore be prioritized across the product portfolio rather than applied with the same intensity to every asset.

A model intended to support early hypothesis generation should not be held to the same performance requirements or governance standards as one expected to influence trial protocol design, monitoring, labeling, or risk minimization decisions.
Additionally, prediction outputs should be embedded within governed workflows rather than treated as stand-alone answers, with clear human oversight checkpoints.

unlisted_practices: Protect against platform dependency through procurement and design controls that preserve internal ownership of key decision frameworks.
Do not treat predictive outputs as validated signals unless they have undergone appropriate scientific and pharmacovigilance review.
Redesign existing processes where needed rather than simply superimposing AI-based prediction on them.
Explicitly define the prediction target, timing, level of application, and intended use before implementing predictive models.
Label exploratory AI findings as such and carry them forward for confirmation.
Represent disease severity, line of therapy, and timing of treatment relative to disease course in predictive models wherever decision relevant.
Define leading indicators for each implementation risk category, with thresholds set locally, assigned ownership, and predefined actions.
Use error injection, deliberately introducing known errors into material for human review, to measure error detection and counter automation complacency.
Establish phenotype governance covering definition, implementation, performance evaluation, versioning, and retirement of exposure and outcome definitions.

screen.reason: This is a framework and perspective article arguing for an enterprise lifecycle evidence ecosystem and governance mitigations for AI-supported predictive drug safety.
